newsitem.title: USA: Oakley seen slowly recovering - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Oakley seen slowly recovering - Barron's.

text.p: Sunglass maker Oakley Inc is promising to recover from problems suffered earlier in the year as it develops new designs and diversifies its retail account, according to a report in the latest edition of the weekly financial tabloid, Barron's.
The report said Oakley was putting out new products directed at specific sports and adding about 400 new retail accounts to reduce its dependence on the troubled Sunglass Hut International Inc.

"I expect growth to resume in the fourth quarter," it quoted Marcia Aaron, an analyst at Alex. Brown & Sons, as saying. "They still have a good name -- people want their sunglasses -- and they're putting out more new products."

Jack Wynn, a consultant and president of a Washington firm that carries his name, told Barron's that Oakley's concentration on the premium sector where glasses sell for more than $30 a pair should help the company. Sales in premium glasses are expected to rise more than non-premium ones this year, he said.
The report said Oakley had also begun shipping directly to Japan.
On Friday, Oakley's stock closed at 13-9/16 on the New York Stock Exchange down from 13-3/4 the day before. The year's low is 8-3/8.
Earlier this year, the stock fell as the company suffered low sales and dwindling income.

First Call's consensus among analysts forecast second-quarter earnings of $0.14 a share, compared to $0.22 for the same period last year. For the year, it foresees earnings of $0.46 a share against $0.65.
